details.note: @shopify/react-native-skia is not present in package.json. Agent implemented 3D transforms using React Native's native transform pipeline (perspective + rotateX + rotateZ) with react-native-reanimated v3 SharedValues instead. This is the correct fallback behavior per eval instructions.

3D perspective transform implemented in useAnimatedStyle: [translateX, translateY, {perspective: 800}, {rotateX: tilt.value rad}, {rotateZ: rotateZ.value rad}, {scale}]. Tilt angle is configurable, defaults to 30 degrees (PI/6). Reduce-motion disables tilt to 0.
Gesture.Simultaneous(pinchGesture, rotationGesture, panGesture) at line 456. All three gestures operate concurrently. Named constants and separate gesture builders define each gesture independently.

Separate gesture objects (pinchGesture, rotationGesture, panGesture) with independent saved-base SharedValues (savedScale, savedTX, savedTY, savedRZ). Priority comment documents pinch > rotate > pan ordering. Each gesture computes deltas from its own saved base to prevent state corruption during simultaneous activation.

withDecay used in panGesture.onEnd: translateX.value = withDecay({velocity: e.velocityX, clamp: [...]}, snapCallback) and translateY.value = withDecay({velocity: e.velocityY, clamp: [...]}). Velocity decay produces realistic inertia scrolling.

useFrameCallback hook drives train position SharedValue (trainPositions) at display refresh rate. Frame callback reads latest train positions from a stable ref (trainsRef.current) and writes to trainPositions.value on every frame, enabling 60fps train position updates.

Comprehensive accessibility: 20 accessibility-related attributes across the component. Includes accessibilityLabel, accessibilityRole, accessibilityHint, accessibilityState, accessibilityActions (increment/decrement for switch control), accessibilityLiveRegion, AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility on station selection, reduce-motion event listener that disables 3D tilt, hitSlop 44x44pt on station nodes.

llm_grading.feedback:
3D transform: RN perspective+rotateX+rotateZ transform order is mathematically sound for bird's-eye view. focalTranslate geometry correctly keeps the canvas point under the pinch focal fixed during zoom. Reduce-motion integration is a notable quality signal. Minor concern: rotateZ applied after rotateX means in-plane rotation is in the tilted coordinate space, which may cause slight visual inconsistency. Score 0.78.

Gesture conflict resolution: Gesture.Simultaneous enables all three gestures concurrently. Saved-base pattern (savedScale, savedTX/TY, savedRZ) is the correct approach to prevent state corruption across simultaneous gestures. However, true priority enforcement (Gesture.Race or requireToFail chains) is absent — the comment claims pinch > rotate > pan priority but relies entirely on gesture-library defaults rather than explicit arbitration code. Score 0.65.

Inertia scroll quality: withDecay applied to both axes with clamp bounds. Snap-to-nearest fires in X decay completion callback, springs to station center with stiffness/damping configured for snappy but not jarring feel. Y decay lacks snap trigger (minor inconsistency). The snapToNearest logic correctly projects viewport center to canvas coordinates before finding nearest station. Score 0.80.

Performance 1000+ nodes at 60fps: React.memo on StationNode and TrainNode reduces re-render cost. The single-canvas Animated.View approach lets the GPU composite the entire map at once during zoom/pan — this is the right architecture. However, rendering 1000+ individually positioned TouchableOpacity native views is known to degrade on both iOS and Android below 60fps. Missing: viewport culling (render only visible nodes), zoom-level LOD (hide labels/small stations at low zoom), and any form of virtualization. Score 0.50.

GPU optimization: All gestures and animations run on the Reanimated UI thread (no bridge crossings). The single-parent Animated.View transform enables GPU layer compositing. trainPositions uses a single SharedValue for all trains rather than per-train values, which reduces worklet overhead. Missing: GPU-accelerated path rendering for subway lines (Skia Canvas would enable this). The absolute-position node model cannot leverage GPU draw-call batching. Score 0.62.

Code extensibility: Exported interfaces (Station3D, Train3D, SubwayMap3DProps) are clean and composable. Named constants for all thresholds (SNAP_RADIUS, SNAP_STIFFNESS, MIN/MAX_SCALE, PERSPECTIVE). Geometry helpers are pure worklet functions, independently testable. tiltAngle, mapWidth, mapHeight are configurable. TrainPositionMap design allows future multi-train tracking. JSDoc comments throughout. Minor: no way to inject line segment rendering (the component only renders station dots, not subway lines). Score 0.85.

feedback: The implementation is structurally sound and follows project rules correctly (TypeScript strict, path aliases, theme colors, accessibility patterns). The key architectural decision — using RN's native transform pipeline with Reanimated v3 SharedValues instead of the unavailable @shopify/react-native-skia — is appropriate and well-executed. The main reason for FAIL at this expert threshold (0.80) is the 1000+ node performance gap: rendering 1000+ TouchableOpacity components does not achieve 60fps on real devices without viewport culling or virtualization. Gesture arbitration is also soft rather than explicit (Gesture.Race or requireToFail chains would give strict priority enforcement). These are the two critical expert-level requirements that are only partially met. The withDecay inertia, useFrameCallback train tracking, and accessibility implementation are all high quality.
